skill.name: version-planner
skill.description: Break product ideas into staged version plans, from a focused MVP to a release-ready V1.0 roadmap.
skill.summary: Create practical MVP and version roadmaps for product ideas.
skill.author: yunshu0909

content.value_statement: Product ideas often grow too large before teams know what to build first. This skill turns requirements into a staged MVP and version roadmap with clear validation points.
actual_capabilities: Ask clarifying questions about pain points, users, required features, constraints, and unknowns.
Extract core value, target users, feature lists, and feature dependencies from a product idea.
Split work into V0.1 MVP, iterative V0.2 to V0.5 releases, and V1.0 readiness.
Define validation points and explicit out-of-scope items for each planned version.
Generate a structured version planning document with next actions and open questions.
limitations: It does not perform market research or validate customer demand by itself.
It does not estimate delivery dates with project management accuracy.
It does not replace technical architecture, security review, or implementation planning.
It depends on user-provided requirements and constraints for useful prioritization.

use_cases.title: Shape a New Product MVP
use_cases.description: Turn a broad product idea into the smallest version that can validate the main user problem.

use_cases.title: Prioritize a Feature Backlog
use_cases.description: Group requested features into staged releases with dependencies, exclusions, and validation goals.

use_cases.title: Prepare Build Scope
use_cases.description: Create a version plan that developers can use before architecture design or sprint planning.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Simple MVP
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request with a rough product idea.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me split this product idea into versions. The idea is: [describe product]. Ask me any key questions first.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Roadmap from Requirements
prompt_templates.scenario: User has a feature list and needs staged releases.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a V0.1 to V1.0 version plan for these requirements: [feature list]. Include what each version will not do.

prompt_templates.title: Refine an Existing Roadmap
prompt_templates.scenario: User has a draft plan that needs clearer scope.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this version plan and improve the sequence, validation points, and dependency order: [draft plan].

prompt_templates.title: Plan Under Constraints
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced planning with technical and business limits.
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a staged roadmap for [product] with these constraints: [platform, team size, timeline, technical limits]. Identify risks and open questions.

output_examples.input: I want to build a local habit tracker with reminders, charts, tags, and cloud sync.
output_examples.output: V0.1 focuses on creating habits and marking daily completion. V0.2 adds local history and basic charts. V0.3 adds reminders. Cloud sync stays out of scope until the core habit loop is validated.

output_examples.input: Our team wants to launch a client portal with messages, files, payments, analytics, and admin roles.
output_examples.output: The first release validates secure client access, project status, and basic file sharing. Later releases add messaging, payments, analytics, and role controls after the portal proves daily use.

output_examples.input: I have a feature list but do not know what belongs in the MVP.
output: Identify the single user problem that must be solved first.
Separate required workflow steps from convenience features.
Move polish, integrations, and advanced settings into later versions.

best_practices: Provide the core pain point, target user, required features, and known constraints before asking for a roadmap.
Keep each version focused on one clear outcome and one validation point.
Review the out-of-scope list before starting implementation.
anti_patterns: Asking for every feature to ship in the MVP without priority tradeoffs.
Using the roadmap as a fixed delivery commitment before technical review.
Skipping clarification when the product idea is still vague.

faq.question: What does this skill produce?
faq.answer: It produces a staged version planning document with an MVP, later releases, validation points, exclusions, open questions, and next actions.

faq.question: Can it help when my idea is vague?
faq.answer: Yes. It first asks clarifying questions about pain points, target users, required features, constraints, and uncertain details.

faq.question: Does it create technical architecture?
faq.answer: No. It can record technical assumptions, but detailed architecture should be handled in a separate design step.

faq.question: Does it estimate exact timelines?
faq.answer: No. It can discuss rough effort, but exact timelines require team capacity, implementation details, and delivery risks.

faq.question: Who should use this skill?
faq.answer: Founders, product managers, solo builders, and developers can use it to reduce scope and plan staged releases.

faq.question: How does it handle too many requested features?
faq.answer: It separates must-have features from later improvements and defines what each version should not include.
